extra.message: User-controlled input req.body.login is concatenated directly into a raw SQL string executed via db.sequelize.query(). An attacker can inject SQL to read/modify arbitrary data (e.g. ' OR '1'='1).

User-controlled req.body.address is concatenated into a shell command passed to child_process.exec() without sanitization or argument escaping. An attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands (e.g. '; cat /etc/passwd').
File upload data is passed to node-serialize's unserialize() with no validation. node-serialize is known to be vulnerable to remote code execution via crafted serialized objects (CVE-2017-5941).

XML from an uploaded file is parsed with libxmljs.parseXmlString using {noent:true}, which enables external entity resolution. An attacker can upload XML with external entities to read local files (XXE).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User-controlled req.body.eqn is passed directly to mathjs.eval(). The mathjs expression parser can evaluate arbitrary JavaScript via its import/constructor gadgets, leading to code execution.
req.query.url is passed directly to res.redirect() without validation. This endpoint is also unauthenticated (routes/app.js line 48), allowing open redirect / phishing.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: userEditSubmit looks up the target user by the client-supplied req.body.id rather than req.user.id. Any authenticated user can modify another user's name, email, and password by changing the id field, leading to account takeover.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Password reset token is computed as md5(req.query.login), which is trivially predictable for any known username. An attacker can forge the reset token and take over any account (also present at line 78 in resetPwSubmit).

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: Admin endpoints (/app/admin/usersapi and /app/admin/users) are protected only by isAuthenticated, not by an admin role check. The admin flag in the view merely hides UI; any authenticated user can call the users API directly.
listUsersAPI returns db.User.findAll() with no attribute filtering, exposing all user records including password hashes to any authenticated user via /app/admin/usersapi.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: output.searchTerm (derived from req.body.name in productSearch) is rendered with <%- %> (unescaped), allowing reflected XSS.
Product fields (id, name, code, tags, description) are rendered with <%- %> (unescaped). These fields are set from user input via modifyProductSubmit with no sanitization, allowing stored XSS.
User-controlled fields (users[i].id, name, email) are inserted into the DOM via innerHTML without escaping. Names/emails are user-controllable through registration/useredit, enabling stored XSS.

Session is configured with a hardcoded secret ('keyboard cat'), cookie secure:false, and saveUninitialized/resave true. The hardcoded secret allows session forgery and the cookie is transmitted without the Secure flag.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: No CSRF protection is applied to any route. csurf is listed in package.json but never used. All state-changing POST endpoints (usersearch, ping, products, modifyproduct, useredit, bulkproducts, resetpw) are vulnerable to CSRF.
